name: Ample, Individual-Pair, and Factor-Complex Equivalence
hypotheses: Finite nonempty binary class; the nonzero-divisor condition holds over every coefficient field.
statement: A class is ample exactly when every paired literal difference is individually regular on its original signed-pattern ring, and exactly when its polar and factor complexes coincide. Thus individual regularity already implies that all paired differences form a regular sequence in every order.
proof: Ample classes have full paired-difference regularity, hence each difference is regular when placed first. Conversely, if every difference is individually regular, a facet of the polar complex cannot omit both literals of any coordinate: maximality would create a monomial annihilated by that paired difference. Its doubled and single coordinates therefore describe a contained coordinate cube, so every polar facet lies in the factor complex. If the two complexes coincide, the two literals over every shattered support form a polar face and hence lie in a contained-cube face, proving strong shattering. Equality of shattering and strong shattering is ampleness.
